md:
### ACHD: when to intervene, lesion by lesion

| Lesion | Intervene when | Technique and points |
|---|---|---|
| VSD | Qp:Qs at least 1.5:1 with LV volume overload | Only if PA systolic "50% less than systemic" (as printed) and PVR no more than one third of SVR; Eisenmenger: surgery typically contraindicated |
| ASD | Qp:Qs at least 1.5 | Device for secundum up to 38 mm; surgery for primum, sinus venosus, large secundum with poor rims, or with arrhythmias |
| RVOT reconstruction | Pulmonary stenosis or regurgitation (the commonest late problem) | Percutaneous valve (graft rupture about 4%, stent fracture 20%); else annulus-sparing repair; replacement preferred over repair; replacement before 17 linked with normal RV function |
| Ebstein | Worse exercise tolerance, heart failure, cyanosis, sustained arrhythmia, paradoxical stroke, symptomatic TR, pregnancy, resting SpO2 below 90% | Repair preferred |
| Supravalvar AS | Discrete lesion, mean gradient above 50 mmHg | Patch aortoplasty, rarely root replacement |
| Valvar AS or AR | Symptoms; valve area below 0.6 cm²; regular exercise or planned pregnancy; symptomatic moderate or severe AR; EF below 55%; LVESD above 55 mm | Root replacement above 55 mm |
| Subvalvar AS | Mean gradient above 50 mmHg as printed (2025 ACC/AHA: peak 50 or more), symptoms, or moderate or severe AR | Myectomy or myotomy if the valve is kept; 20% recurrence; tunnel: Konno |
| Transposition, RVOT obstruction | Gradient above 60 mmHg or RV/LV pressure ratio above 0.6 | Baffle stenosis: balloon or patch; IVC stenosis urgent, SVC stenosis usually benign |
| Failing Fontan | Pathway obstruction that the catheter cannot treat | Revision with Maze and epicardial pacemaker; otherwise transplant listing, sometimes heart-liver |

Source: summarised from "Adult congenital heart disease: surgical overview" in this tab (TSRA ch. 113).

### Neonatal physiology at a glance

| Feature | What follows |
|---|---|
| High metabolic rate and oxygen consumption | High respiratory rate and cardiac index |
| Limited ability to raise stroke volume or heart rate | Very sensitive to negative inotropes |
| Myocardial metabolism | Favours glucose over fatty acids |
| Poorly developed sarcoplasmic reticulum | Contraction depends on extracellular calcium; hypocalcaemia badly tolerated (hence calcium infusions) |
| Autonomic imbalance | Prone to vagal reflexes |
| Relatively non-compliant lungs, small distal airways | Airways block easily with secretions; prone to respiratory failure |
| Fetal haemoglobin (alpha2 gamma2) until about 6 months | Binds oxygen more avidly; dissociation curve shifted to the left |

Source: summarised from "Neonatal physiology" in this tab (London Deanery teaching 2024).

| Tumour | Where and with what | Course | Management |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rhabdomyoma | Commonest; multiple, ventricular; tuberous sclerosis | Regresses | Operate only for obstruction or arrhythmia |
| Fibroma | Single; ventricular septum or free wall | Does not regress; arrhythmia and sudden death | Resect |
| Teratoma | Pericardial; infancy | Not given in the notes | Not given in the notes |
| Myxoma | Older children; Carney complex | Not given in the notes | Not given in the notes |

### AAOCA: AATS 2017 consensus against the 2025 ACC/AHA adult guideline

| Question | AATS 2017 (written mainly for the young) | ACC/AHA 2025 (adults) |
|---|---|---|
| First imaging | TTE (I, B); then CT coronary angiography or CMR (IIa, B) | Coronary CT angiography (1); MR angiography if CT contraindicated |
| Ischaemia testing | Exercise testing with nuclear perfusion or stress echo (I, B) | Exercise or dobutamine stress (echo, nuclear or MR) preferred to vasodilator stress |
| Symptomatic | Ischaemic chest pain, arrhythmic syncope or aborted sudden death: restrict activity and offer surgery (I, B) | Symptoms or ischaemia attributable to the anomalous artery: surgery (1) |
| Asymptomatic left from right sinus | Interarterial course: offer surgery (I, B); no competitive sport (I, B) | High-risk anatomy: surgery reasonable (2a); without ischaemia otherwise observation or surgery (2b) |
| Asymptomatic right from left sinus | Negative stress imaging: competitive sport after counselling (IIa, C) | Observation or surgery (2b) |
| Operation | Remove the intramural course and any ostial narrowing: unroofing, ostioplasty or reimplantation (I, B); PA translocation as adjunct (IIb, C) | Unroofing with or without ostioplasty, reimplantation, pulmonary translocation; CABG only with coexisting coronary disease |
| Age | Not in the summary read | Sudden death mainly at extreme exertion and under 35; no documented benefit of surgery in asymptomatic middle-aged patients without high-risk features |

Source: summarised from "Anomalous aortic origin of a coronary artery: AATS 2017 recommendations" in this tab and "American ACHD guideline 2025: coronary anomalies, coronary fistula and vascular rings" in Adult congenital.

### Systemic venous anomalies: why each matters

| Anomaly | What it is | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Persistent left SVC | 0.2 to 3% of healthy people, 1.3 to 11% with congenital heart disease; drains to an enlarged coronary sinus; a bridging innominate vein may be absent | Cannulation; retrograde cardioplegia washes out; pacing leads; the Glenn may need to be bilateral |
| Unroofed coronary sinus with left SVC | Occurs with a persistent left SVC | Right-to-left shunt to the left atrium |
| Interrupted IVC with azygos continuation | Occurs with left isomerism | A Glenn then carries almost all venous return (Kawashima) |

Source: summarised from "Systemic venous anomalies" in this tab, with the corrected prevalence from Congenital 12.
